newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Oct 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Oct 15.

text.p: PRAVO - Construction prices increased by an estimated 0.9 percent between August and September.

- Daewoo Avia will export 300 lorries to Poland accrding to a spokesman from the company. The company also recently announced plans to export 300 lorries to Romania, 50 of which have already been delivered.

- The Czech Republic has the smallest area of agricultural land per person of all Central and Eastern European countries with 0.4 hectares. The Czech average of 15.37 hectares per agricultural worker is close to the EU average of 16.86 hectares.
- Ceska Pojistovna opened its first branch office in London on Monday, its first in an EU country.

- The number of airports in the Czech Republic decreased from 78 to 73 last year. Of these, 68 are considered public airports and only four of these are still in state hands this year according to information from the Ministry of Transportation. Airports in Karlovy Vary, Brno and Ostrava should be privatised next year while privatisation of the largest Czech airport, Prague's Ruzyne airport, will not occur in the foreseeable future.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Skoda Plzen posted consolidated pre-tax profits of 450 million crowns in the first six months of 1996, including the 100 million crown losses suffered by Skoda Liaz.

- Czech Agricultural policies are heading in the same direction as the combined agricultural policies in EU countries, Minister of Agriculture, Josef Lux stated after meeting with the EU agricultural commissioner, Franz Fischler.

- The decrease in the dynamic growth of monetary reserves is expected to continue in the future according to Jiri Pospisil from the Czech National Bank. M2 growth has decreased to the target area of 13 to 16 percent, which should have a positive effect on the inflation rate.
- The majority of taxi drivers in Prague are expected to raise their prices to 15 or 16 crowns a kilometre starting Tuesday as taxi prices are deregulated.
